front: What is the basic untagged Ethernet frame size, and what is counted?
back: 64–1518 bytes for the basic 1500-byte-payload framing, destination MAC through FCS. Preamble, SFD, and interframe gap are excluded.

front: What is the data-area size in the basic untagged Ethernet II frame?
back: 46–1500 bytes including any minimum-size padding. The 1500-byte payload limit is distinct from the total Ethernet frame length.

front: What are the Ethernet II header and FCS sizes?
back: Destination MAC 6 + source MAC 6 + EtherType 2 = 14-byte untagged header; FCS adds 4 bytes.

front: Which Ethernet II types distinguish IPv4 from ARP?
back: 0x0800 identifies IPv4; 0x0806 identifies ARP. The EtherType describes the Ethernet payload protocol.

front: Is every frame longer than 1518 bytes invalid?
back: No. VLAN tags and supported larger-frame configurations change valid sizes. Interpret size/error counters against the platform and interface configuration.

front: How long is a MAC address, and what does an OUI identify?
back: 48 bits, or 12 hexadecimal digits. An OUI identifies an organizational allocation; locally assigned MACs and other IEEE allocation sizes also exist.

front: How do you identify an Ethernet group address and broadcast address?
back: The low-order bit of the first octet is set for group addresses. The all-ones broadcast address is ffff.ffff.ffff.

front: What information does ordinary switching learn and look up?
back: Learn source MAC + VLAN → ingress port. Look up destination MAC in the VLAN to forward, filter, or flood.

front: Does unknown-unicast flooding change the destination MAC?
back: No. It copies the unicast frame to eligible forwarding ports in the same VLAN, excluding the ingress port.

front: What refreshes a dynamic MAC entry, and what is the reference 2960 timer?
back: Frames received from that source refresh its location. The documented 2960 IOS 15.0(2)SE default is 300 seconds; verify the actual device.

front: What creates a static MAC entry for a VLAN and interface?
back: mac address-table static H.H.H vlan N interface X. It does not age or disappear in a dynamic-table clear; remove the matching configuration to undo it.

front: How do you clear learned MAC entries without removing static entries?
back: At privileged EXEC: clear mac address-table dynamic. Hosts sending new frames can be learned again immediately.

front: Which columns matter in show mac address-table?
back: VLAN, MAC address, entry type, and port. Read the VLAN first; a dynamic row gives the learned path toward the source.

front: Store-and-forward compared with cut-through?
back: Store-and-forward receives the whole frame and checks FCS before forwarding. Cut-through can start before the complete frame/FCS arrives.

front: How do switch ports and VLANs separate Ethernet domains?
back: Switch ports separate collision domains; full-duplex links have no collisions. A VLAN is a broadcast domain that can span multiple switches.

front: Why can a Layer 2 loop carry repeated flooded traffic?
back: Ordinary Ethernet has no hop-count field to stop circulation. Spanning tree creates a loop-free forwarding topology.

front: MAC address table versus ARP table?
back: MAC table: MAC + VLAN → port. IPv4 ARP table: on-link IP → MAC. Clearing either table does not directly clear the other.

front: Do many MAC addresses on one port prove a fault?
back: No. An uplink can carry many hosts. Compare the topology; repeated moves of one MAC warrant investigation but do not alone identify the cause.

front: Can the Ethernet FCS repair a corrupted frame?
back: No. The CRC detects corruption; it is not error correction. A store-and-forward switch discards a frame that fails its FCS check.

front: A learned host transmits on a new port. Must the old entry age out first?
back: No. With ordinary dynamic learning and no restriction, the new source frame updates its MAC/VLAN location to the new ingress port.
